subject: specifying multiple distributions over a dimensions of a data matrix

messages.author: 33d5534e21fbbe0f
messages.subject: specifying multiple distributions over a dimensions of a data matrix
parts:
Hi stan experts,  I have a data matrix[N3,D3] y3 over where the first D3_bin columns are binary responses and the remaining (D3- D3_bin) responses are ordered.   Since M-H steps are employed based on incrementing lp_ (un-normalized), I assume that the following likelihood specification is okay:

for(d in 1:D3_bin) col(y3,d) ~ bernoulli_logit(col(c3,d)); // vectorized for N3 observations
for(i in 1:N3) for(d in (D3_bin+1):D3) y3[i,d] ~ ordered_logistic(c3[i,d],gamma3[d]);

I'd appreciate having your confirmation, nonetheless.   As always, thank you.

--
Thank you, Terrance Savitsky

messages.subject: Does my model work?
parts:

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Does my model work?
parts:
I'd suggest breaking your data vector y3 into two parts,
y3_bin and y3_ord, with their own lengths D3_bin
and D3_ord.

Then you could vectorize everything more easily, with
your

>> for(d in 1:D3_bin) col(y3,d) ~ bernoulli_logit(col(c3,d)); // vectorized for N3 observations
>> for(i in 1:N3) for(d in (D3_bin+1):D3) y3[i,d] ~ ordered_logistic(c3[i,d],gamma3[d]);

becoming:

y3_bin ~ bernoulli_logit(c3);

for (i in 1:N3_ord) y3_ord[i] ~ ordered_logistic(c3[i],gamma3);

- Bob
